description: LukeEvansTech shared Renovate config — home-operations/renovate-presets plus house defaults. Consume it from any repo with: extends: ["github>LukeEvansTech/renovate-config"].

customManagers.description: Track the doco-cd GitOps controller pinned inside Butane (.bu) provisioning files. On the FCOS boxes (seedbox, cr-nut) the doco-cd container that actually runs is launched by a systemd docker-run unit written in the .bu, NOT by any compose file Renovate reads — so without this the controller version silently drifts. Renovate has no native Butane manager, so extract the image tag by regex and resolve it as a docker dependency (digest pinned via docker:pinDigests like everything else).

packageRules.description: Semantic update-type labels. Consumers key automation off these: the renovate-review.yaml breaking-change gate ungates type/digest and renovate/github-action so low-blast-radius bumps skip the (paid) AI review entirely. Before this existed only talos-cluster declared them locally, so the same workflow copied into nut-apps/seedbox-apps silently gated EVERY PR — the ungate branch was unreachable and every action bump ran a full Opus review. addLabels (not labels) is deliberate: it is additive, so the house `dependencies` label and vulnerabilityAlerts' `security` label survive alongside these.
pin/pinDigest are included alongside digest — they are equally low-blast-radius and the digest automerge rule below already treats all three alike, so the review gate should ungate them all.

Auto-merge minor/patch everywhere after a 2-day soak — CI-gated PR merge. platformAutomerge:false means Renovate self-gates on CI and self-merges, so no branch-protection ruleset is needed, and repos with zero CI checks never auto-merge (Renovate requires ignoreTests:true to merge without tests). github-actions and mise bumps land here too: they are deliberately NOT branch-merged, because every managed repo's baseline-main-protection ruleset has a pull_request rule that blocks direct pushes to main, so automergeType:branch fails with 'Unknown error when attempting branch automerge'. Majors never match any rule here, so they always stay manual. Repos add their own protected-package denylist (automerge:false, last-match-wins) for anything that must stay human-reviewed.

Container images (docker datasource) opt out of the soak for minor/patch: GHCR/quay and most non-Docker-Hub registries expose no reliable release timestamp, so minimumReleaseAge never turns green and versioned bumps stall indefinitely (truenas-apps node-exporter/doco-cd sat pending 9-17 days). Every image is digest-pinned via docker:pinDigests and CI still gates the PR merge, so this reuses the same trust model the digest/pin rule already relies on. Overrides the 2-day soak above (last-match-wins); automerge:true is inherited from that rule.

Auto-merge digest and pin updates — CI-gated, deliberately NO minimumReleaseAge: mutable-tag digest bumps reset the age clock on every upstream rebuild and GHCR often has no per-digest timestamp, so an age gate leaves digest PRs pending forever (talos-cluster had 11 pending up to 19 days).

Majors stay 100% manual AND no longer open a PR: they queue behind a checkbox on each repo's Dependency Dashboard under 'Pending Approval'. Majors never matched any automerge rule, so assignAutomerge:false always assigned them — 146 open major PRs across the estate were the single largest source of notification email, and each also re-ran CI on every rebase. Ticking the dashboard box creates the PR on the next run, so nothing is lost and the backlog stays visible in one place per repo. Security majors are exempt: vulnerabilityAlerts sets dependencyDashboardApproval:false so vulnerability-driven updates still raise a PR immediately.

Never pin the codelooks-com/terraform-workflows reusable workflows that are tracked on @main. The two Azure Terraform repos (terraform-azure-platform, terraform-azure-workloads) reference standard-ci/-cd/-drift at @main on purpose: their GitHub OIDC subject includes job_workflow_ref, so the Azure federated credentials only trust a token whose sub ends in .../standard-*.yaml@refs/heads/main. SHA-pinning the ref rewrites that claim to @<sha>, no federated credential matches, and every plan/apply/drift run fails auth with AADSTS700213 (already reverted once in terraform-azure-workloads #18). Scoped to currentValue main so the other repos that pin standard-* to a @<sha> # vX.Y.Z tag keep their normal version-bump flow.

Never digest-pin docker images referenced inside GitHub Actions workflows. In this estate such an image is the repo's OWN build target: its name lives in a workflow env (IMAGE: ghcr.io/<org>/<repo>) and is composed into the push tags as ${IMAGE}:${version}. docker:pinDigests appends @sha256:… to it, turning the push reference into an invalid 'repo@sha256:…:tag' that buildx rejects — breaking every release build. This bit todoist-sort (build.yml, via #14) and was pre-empted per-repo in packer-vsphere; centralising it here lets both drop their local enabled:false workaround and protects future repos. Only docker-datasource deps in workflows are affected: GitHub Action SHA pinning is a separate mechanism (helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests) and is untouched, and Dockerfile/compose/k8s FROM lines are still digest-pinned by their own managers. Scoped by manager+datasource because the github-actions manager is the only one that reads .github/workflows/*.yml.

Terraform/Terragrunt-managed deps never auto-merge: in the codelooks-com IaC repos a merge to main auto-applies via CD, so provider/module bumps stay human-reviewed. Actions and mise bumps in those repos still auto-merge via the rules above.

doco-cd is the GitOps controller that deploys every stack — a bad bump breaks the deployer itself and can't self-heal, and its authoritative pin usually lives in a Butane (.bu) unit that only takes effect on a box re-provision. Never auto-merge it (overrides the container rules above, last-match-wins) and group every doco-cd update — the bootstrap compose and the .bu pin — into a single manual PR so both files move together.

The Butane (.bu) doco-cd customManager tracks image versions only — never append a digest. docker:pinDigests would rewrite the systemd docker-run line to tag@sha256:… and the customManager digest-pin step fails on it ('Error updating branch: update failure'); a re-provision resolves the tag and the compose copy already carries the digest, so version-only here is both sufficient and what actually works. Scoped to matchManagers custom.regex (the only regex customManager is the .bu one) — the same manager-scoped approach as the Flux OCIRepository pinDigests:false carve-out; matchFileNames does not scope customManager-extracted deps.
